questions.stem: Which output device is specifically designed to produce large-format, high-precision technical drawings such as engineering blueprints and architectural plans?

options.option_text: Inkjet printer — sprays liquid ink droplets onto paper
Plotter — draws precise lines using pens or cutting heads
Dot matrix printer — uses impact pins striking an inked ribbon
Laser printer — fuses toner powder onto paper using heat

questions.explanation: B is correct. A plotter moves a pen (or cutting head) along X-Y axes to draw continuous vector lines, making it the standard tool for CAD blueprints and maps. Inkjet and laser printers render raster images by depositing dots — unsuitable for the continuous line precision required in engineering drawings. Dot matrix printers are impact-based and used for multi-copy forms, not large-format precision work.

questions.stem: An OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) sheet reader used in competitive exam evaluation works on which underlying physical principle?

options.option_text: Magnetic field variations caused by pencil graphite deposits
Differential light reflectance from darkened bubble regions
Electrical conductivity change in pencil-marked paper areas
Infrared heat signature from high-pressure pen or pencil marks

questions.explanation: B is correct. OMR devices shine a beam of light onto the answer sheet; darkened (filled) bubbles absorb more light and reflect less back to the sensor, while blank regions reflect more. This difference in reflectance is detected and interpreted as a mark. Option A (magnetic field) is the principle behind MICR used in bank cheques, not OMR. Option C (conductivity) describes touch-screen technology, not OMR. Option D (infrared heat) has no role in passive paper scanning.

questions.stem: A dial-up modem was essential for early internet connectivity over telephone lines. Which paired function made this possible?

options.option_text: Compressing digital packets into smaller binary bursts for faster transfer
Modulating outgoing digital signals into analog and demodulating received analog back to digital
Encrypting data using RSA public-key pairs before telephone line transmission
Amplifying weakened electrical signals to prevent degradation across phone cables

questions.explanation: B is correct. The word 'modem' is a portmanteau of MOdulator-DEModulator. Phone lines carry analog signals; computers generate digital data. The modem modulates (digital→analog) at the sender and demodulates (analog→digital) at the receiver. Option A (compression) is a separate protocol layer, not the modem's core function. Option C (RSA encryption) is handled by software/SSL, not the modem hardware. Option D (amplification) is the job of a repeater or signal booster.

questions.stem: Which statement most accurately describes the role of L1/L2/L3 cache memory in a modern processor?

options.option_text: Stores the operating system kernel permanently even when power is removed
Acts as high-speed SRAM buffers between the CPU and slower main RAM
Extends available RAM by mapping inactive data to hard disk swap space
Holds BIOS firmware instructions executed during the POST startup sequence

questions.explanation: B is correct. Cache memory (built from fast SRAM) sits between the CPU and main RAM (DRAM). Because RAM access takes ~100 CPU cycles, the cache pre-fetches frequently used data, reducing the average memory-access latency. L1 is fastest and smallest (inside the core), L2 is larger, L3 is shared across cores. Option A describes ROM/Flash (non-volatile storage). Option C describes virtual memory — a software technique using the HDD/SSD. Option D describes the BIOS chip (ROM), not cache.

questions.stem: A digitizer tablet (graphics tablet) is distinct from a touchscreen because it primarily performs which function in professional design workflows?

options.option_text: Converts scanned physical documents into editable text using OCR algorithms
Records audio input and converts it into digital waveform sample files
Translates stylus position and pressure into precise XY coordinate data streams
Displays colour-accurate high-resolution images for professional colour proofing

questions.explanation: C is correct. A digitizer tablet uses an electromagnetic grid beneath its surface to track the stylus's exact X-Y position and pressure level, sending this as vector coordinate data to the software. This enables smooth, pressure-sensitive line work impossible with a mouse. Unlike a touchscreen (capacitive, detects finger touch), it works through the surface and responds only to its paired stylus. Option A describes an OCR scanner. Option B describes a microphone/ADC. Option D describes a colour-calibrated display, not an input device.

questions.stem: A double-conversion online UPS differs fundamentally from a line-interactive UPS in which way that makes it preferred for sensitive data centre servers?

options.option_text: It regulates voltage fluctuations using an autotransformer without touching the AC waveform
It continuously converts incoming AC to DC then back to AC, fully isolating the load from mains
It transfers to battery power only after detecting a complete power outage condition
It filters high-frequency electromagnetic interference injected by other equipment on the supply

questions.explanation: B is correct. In a double-conversion (online) UPS, power always flows: Mains AC → Rectifier (AC→DC) → Inverter (DC→AC) → Load. The load NEVER runs directly off the mains, so any sag, surge, or outage is absorbed invisibly — zero transfer time. A line-interactive UPS (Option A) uses an autotransformer to correct voltage but only switches to inverter on outage, meaning a brief transfer gap. Option C describes a standby (offline) UPS — the cheapest type with the longest transfer time (~8 ms). Option D is a noise filter/conditioner, not a UPS variant.

questions.stem: A storage administrator selects RAID-5 over RAID-1 for a four-drive server array. Which trade-off is the administrator explicitly accepting?

options.option_text: Write performance improves because parity is pre-calculated before disk commits
Usable capacity rises to (N−1) drives, but a second failure during rebuild causes total data loss
Full mirroring is maintained while parity provides an additional recovery layer
All four drives are striped without redundancy, doubling throughput over RAID-5

questions.explanation: B is correct. RAID-5 stripes data with distributed parity across N drives, giving (N−1) drives of usable space (3 drives out of 4 = 75% efficiency). It tolerates ONE drive failure. During the rebuild phase, however, all remaining drives are under heavy read stress — if any second drive fails during this window, the entire array is lost. RAID-1 mirrors data (only 50% efficiency) but survives multiple failures as long as one mirror remains. Option A is wrong: RAID-5 write performance is SLOWER than RAID-0/1 because parity must be computed on every write. Option C describes no real RAID level — RAID-5 does NOT maintain full mirroring. Option D describes RAID-0, which has zero fault tolerance.
